Here too, Rav Huna is referring to a case where
a certain … child who learned … Avoda Zara when … six years … raised a dilemma to him: … What is … to tread
a certain outstanding child who learned the tractate of Avoda Zara when he was six years old. People raised a dilemma to him: What is the halakha? Is it permitted to tread
in the winepress … with the gentile?
in the winepress … with the gentile, … But doesn’t … render … a libation … with his hands, … where we tie his hands … But doesn’t … render … a libation … with … foot? … Rendering

in the winepress together with the gentile, in accordance with the ruling of the mishna. They asked the child: But doesn’t the gentile render the wine a libation by touching it with his hands, rendering it forbidden? If so, how may a Jew derive benefit from the wine by receiving payment for his work? The child replied: It is permitted in a case where we tie his hands so that he cannot pour the wine as a libation. The child was then asked: But doesn’t the gentile render the wine a libation by touching it with his foot? The child replied: Rendering
